chapter_note: Heavy damage (85%) obscures most of the chapter. The substrate teaching is concentrated in two parallel five-fold mappings: the beautiful tree as Father with five members (reflection/mind/thought/counsel/teaching → cosmic figures: Third Ambassador, First Man, Great Mind, Pillar) at i=108-148, and the bitter tree as Satan with parallel inverted five members (reflection=law of death, counsel=exchange, teaching=furnaces, thought=stronghold, mind=bolos) at i=177-184. The Manichaean editorial frame imports the Gospel parable of two trees as the dialogue prompt (i=9-13), polemicizes against rival doctrines (i=20-24, i=78-98), and inserts ecclesial categories (Church, catechumens) into the cosmic mapping at i=120-121, 128, 136-137. The opening dialogue and Gospel citation are unmistakably late.
